newsitem.title: NEPAL: Jockeying delays new government in Nepal.
newsitem.headline: Jockeying delays new government in Nepal.

text.p: Manoeuvring by coalition partners over the spoils of office delayed the formation of a new government in the Himalayan kingdom of Nepal, political leaders said on Tuesday.

Lokesh Bahadur Chand of the centre-right Rashtriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) said he would take office on Wednesday instead of Tuesday as planned because the new three-party coalition was still debating the make-up of the cabinet.
"There is no problem but discussions have to be held," Chand told Reuters in the capital Kathmandu. "It (swearing-in) will now be held tomorrow."

Party officials in Chand's three-party coalition, dominated by the former royalist RPP and the communist United Marxist Leninist (UML) party, said they were engaged in intensive debate over the government.
Chand said the new coalition government would follow a liberal economic policy but protect the poor. About 42 percent of the kingdom's 21 million people live in poverty.
The new government will welcome foreign investment and fight corruption, he said.
Chand, 57, said initially the cabinet would have fewer than the 47 ministers in outgoing prime minister Sher Bahadur Deuba's government. Later it would be expanded, he said.
Chand said he would announce his cabinet on Wednesday, when he was expected to take oath at the Narayanhity Palace. "Final distribution of ministries is yet to be decided," he said.
King Birendra invited Chand to be the new prime minister on Monday, five days after a coalition led by Deuba's centrist Nepali Congress party lost a confidence motion in parliament.

Deuba's coalition fell largely as a result of a split in the RPP, which had earlier provided support to the Congress party while the communists sat in the opposition. Deuba resigned last Thursday but has stayed on as caretaker prime minister.
Chand leads a group of 10 deputies from his RPP, which has a total of 19 members in the 205-seat parliament.
UML, which has 90 deputies and is likely to dominate the new government, was divided over its nominees in the new government.
"There is no unanimity in the standing committee about the party's nominees to join the new government," UML official Pradeep Nepal said.

The centrist Nepal Sadbhavana Party (NSP) was a minor partner with two deputies. One lawmaker from the communist Nepal Workers and Peasants Party (NWPP) has pledged to support the coalition, giving it 103 votes -- just enough to survive.
Deuba's coalition was undermined by corruption charges and the RPP's allegations that Nepali Congress centralised powers.
The UML had held power from November 1994, when inconclusive general elections were held, until September 1995 when Deuba engineered the communists' downfall.
Chand would be Nepal's fifth prime minister since multi-party democracy under a constitutional monarch was established in 1990 after a bloody pro-democracy movement.

He served twice as prime minister under the Panchayat system of partyless government which lasted from 1961 to 1990 and was fiercely opposed by the communists. The RPP was constituted by leaders of the former partyless rule.
The next general election is not scheduled until 1999.
